Name: Tarentum, Gateway of Southern Italy: The Inner-Sea Harbor and the Citadel Passage
RagShortTexts: Tarentum commands the Mare Piccolo, a naturally enclosed harbor, and is a wealthy home of Greek sailors and merchants
Young nobles opened a water gate at night and let Hannibal storm the city, but Roman survivors held the clifftop citadel
In 209 BC Fabius used a ruse to turn the garrison commander, retook Tarentum, and plundered it on a vast scale
BaseText: Tarentum (town_rome_tarentum) is the only city-state founded by Spartan colonists in southern Italy, and it guards the narrows at the northern end of the Gulf of Tarentum. The city possesses an almost completely enclosed, calm inner sea, the 'Little Sea' (Mare Piccolo), reached only through a narrow channel, which makes it the ultimate naval harbor for controlling the Ionian Sea and the sea routes to Greece. In 212 BC, pro-Carthaginian young nobles of Tarentum deceived the gate guards by pretending to return from a night hunt, and led Hannibal's hidden troops into the city, where they slaughtered the Roman garrison. The Roman fortress commander, however, fell back with his best men to the isolated clifftop citadel on a jutting headland, and with stone-throwing catapults sealed off the mouth of the Little Sea completely, so that the Carthaginian warships could not leave the harbor. In 209 BC the elder Fabius, using agents inside the citadel and a ruse, turned the Bruttian mercenaries in the garrison, successfully recovered Tarentum, and seized three thousand talents of gold and countless bronze statues.

Variants.Content: We struggle to survive between the iron heel of the Roman barbarians and the false promises of Carthage. Fabius's legions stripped the golden crown of Aphrodite from our temple like bandits!

General Fabius the Elder recovered Tarentum through patience and cunning! The traitors believed Hannibal could protect them, and in the end they could only die under the counterattack of the citadel garrison.
General Hannibal even designed with his own hands an overland slipway to haul the warships into the Little Sea, but the weakness of the mercenaries betrayed this great naval harbor.
